record_type: exhaustive structured parse over frozen R03 aperture

parse_units.content: Information-theoretic framework for modeling computational progress as transitions in search-space accessibility.
Paradigm shifts are predicted to show increases in aligned information velocity before accessibility and capability: ΔΛ_E -> Δα -> ΔC, with t_Λ < t_α < t_C and bounded horizon t_C-t_Λ<τ.

Framework is falsified if major capability transitions routinely occur without preceding increases in aligned information velocity; valid tests require measurable Λ_E, later accessibility, later capability, and bounded delay. Source also limits claim: not every search-efficiency increase creates a revolution.

Theory and measurement protocol are defined; current phase is empirical validation through historical case studies and proxy reconstruction; listed initial targets include compilers, autodiff, tensor frameworks, and transformers.
Technological progress is framed as transformation of search processes rather than primarily accumulation of computational resources; discontinuities occur when search structure changes.
Defines Ω_t=(Cfrak_t, α_t, g_t, n_t, U_t) and source meanings for computational context, accessibility field, search geometry, searchable dimensionality, and utility structure.

Proposes stochastic capability evolution model coupling accessibility, latent capability gradients and stochastic discovery; source explicitly states it is proposed for empirical investigation, not assumed physical law.

Models accessibility using representational distance, iteration time/cost, information, alignment, tooling maturity, economic accessibility and prior attention; defines D_R, T_M and E_A with examples.

Defines aligned information velocity Λ_E, information gain I(H;O), and utility alignment A(U|O,Cfrak); states experiments may be valuable by eliminating possibilities and distinguishes aligned information from benchmark gaming or irrelevant optimization.

Defines χ:(g,n,U)->(g',n',U'), metric transformation χ_g, dimensional transformation χ_n, and structural detection criterion using description-length reduction and accessibility; source claims genuine breakthrough absorbs complexity previously carried externally.
Predicts ΔI -> ΔA -> ΔΛ_E -> Δα -> ΔC; distinguishes resource scaling from structural change by leverage ratio; proposes stochastic Ω evolution with exploitation, structural and stochastic terms.

Primary empirical prediction requires increasing Λ_E before accessibility acceleration and capability within pre-specified τ; source says framework remains an empirical hypothesis requiring historical datasets, proxy reconstruction and falsification testing.
Defines empirical objective and tested causal ordering ΔΛ_E -> Δα -> ΔC with bounded delay; distinguishes resource scaling from χ structural transformations.
Specifies Ω_t measurement variables and operational Λ_E components, with historical proxies for information gain, utility alignment and iteration cost.

Uses exponential accessibility model with D_R, T_M, E_A, P_A; explicitly labels exponential form an initial operational model and permits alternative functional forms during validation; goal is relative change estimation rather than direct accessibility measurement.
Operational χ criterion requires description-length reduction, accessibility increase, and excess over background compression; examples include compilers, autodiff and tensor frameworks.
Requires positive cases, false-positive cases and false-negative cases; false positives calibrate selection/alignment failures, false negatives are described as strongest falsification test.

parse_units.section: Proxy Estimation Limits + Temporal Validation + Falsification Criteria
parse_units.content: Lists historical proxy uncertainties; specifies six-step temporal validation including pre-defined domain τ; lists five rejection conditions including ordering, resource explanation, description length, false positives and post-hoc τ adjustment.

Causal variables, proxies, validation protocol and falsification criteria are defined; remaining tasks are dataset construction, Λ_E trajectory estimation, precursor comparison and predictive-performance evaluation.
States theory must be able to fail; central commitment is Λ_E before capability; framework fails if major transitions consistently have t_C<=t_Λ after uncertainty/proxy accounting.

Defines false negative as major capability without measurable Λ_E increase and false positive as Λ_E increase without capability after τ; repeated cases threaten necessity or sufficiency claims respectively.

parse_units.section: Temporal Horizon, Resource Scaling, Description Length, Alignment, Geometry
parse_units.content: Defines failure tests for post-hoc horizon extension, resource-only explanations, absent description-length reduction, inadequate alignment discrimination, and transitions lacking measurable geometry/accessibility change.
Requires multi-domain validity, added predictive value beyond selection pressure, and prospective ranking performance above random/resource/investment/trend baselines.

Survival requires precursor ordering, bounded lead, resource-control survival, manageable false positives and cross-domain signal; conclusion reiterates capability explosions as downstream consequences and says contrary evidence should reject framework.
Phase Boundary Dataset is described as empirical foundation for testing whether paradigm transitions are preceded by aligned information velocity under bounded τ.

Dataset is designed to track search-process structure, including hypothesis-feedback velocity, accessibility, description-length reduction, evaluation efficiency and utility alignment, not only outcome metrics.
Represents each historical transition as M_old -> M_new and evaluates transition for structural change.

Defines case schema fields for identity, old/new mechanisms, intervention/information/accessibility/capability timestamps, metrics, resources, outcome classification, uncertainty/evidence quality and sources.

Treats manual derivatives -> autodiff as candidate phase transition; proposes complexity transfer from human derivative reasoning to computational substrate; explicitly distinguishes autodiff from backpropagation and narrows transition target.

parse_units.section: Previous Regime + Search Bottleneck + Structural Intervention
parse_units.content: Describes manual derivation/implementation/debugging bottleneck and changed workflow after automatic gradient generation.
Predicts ΔL_χ>0, ΔΛ_E>0 and Δα>0 through reduced implementation/debugging/verification burden and lower representational distance.
Specifies expected temporal sequence and candidate proxies for information gain, iteration cost, description length and accessibility.

parse_units.section: Alternative Explanations + Falsification + Current Assessment + Status
parse_units.content: Lists hardware, dataset and algorithmic alternatives with controls; gives six weakening conditions; classifies autodiff as candidate χ_g transition and says historical validation remains required.
Classifies autodiff as strong candidate; hypothesizes derivative complexity absorption; describes manual regime and AD intervention/milestones.
Source asserts support for description-length absorption, iteration-efficiency increase and search-geometry expansion, with specific claimed effects.
Reports milestone periods and τ≈years as consistent with bounded transition; acknowledges compute/data contributions and distinguishes AD from existence of gradients.

Source says evidence does not strongly support false-negative failure, says compute was necessary but insufficient, rates criteria mostly positive with compute/data confound and concludes case provides positive evidence for CPB mechanism.
Classifies assembly -> compilers as strong candidate and hypothesizes low-level execution complexity absorption into compiler layer; gives historical examples.
Source maps transition to description-length absorption, increased iteration velocity and expanded search basin through lower representational distance.
Claims compilers enabled broad software domains; acknowledges hardware as necessary contributor but argues compiler abstraction multiplies resource usefulness.
Rates structural mechanism criteria positive with hardware confound and concludes assembly -> compilers supports recurring CPB pattern.
Tests whether major capability can arise without prior structural Λ_E increase; identifies entangled compute/data/scaling as high-risk falsification regime.

Describes pre-2012 structural substrate, AlexNet, architectural refinement and foundation-model scaling; source says immediate χ precursor is ambiguous and later gains increasingly resemble resource-driven basin exploitation.
Rates ΔL evidence mixed, ΔΛ strong but temporally ambiguous, Δα mixed; documents strong compute/data/capital confounds.
Finds partially yes to capability without clear prior Λ_E and to resource-dominant explanations; classifies mixed/weak falsification pressure and says CPB weaker for mature optimization regimes.

Proposes distinction between basin-opening χ events and basin-mining regimes, with causal structure χ event -> expanded basin -> resource exploitation -> capability growth; source says framework survives with refinement.

Adversarial synthetic sweep of 1000 transitions varies resource dominance, structural signal, proxy noise and ordering; break criteria include ordering violation, unbounded τ or >=70% resource explanation.
Reports 77% break/falsification rate overall and ~89% in high-resource-dominance scenarios; describes resource-driven growth, basin mining and temporal-ordering collapse.
Source calls test strongest adversarial pressure so far and says CPB explains foundational abstractions better than mature high-resource regimes.
Requires basin-opening/exploitation regime detection, structural-stack accounting, and context-dependent τ; narrows strongest claim to phase boundaries rather than all capability improvements.
Classifies strong falsification pressure—model survives with refinement; ordering weak under scaling; regime distinction required; identifies boundary of CPB applicability.

Tests CPB classification on 20 historical transitions against common historical interpretations, with 50% random binary agreement baseline; source calls process independent CPB classification but no live raters are part of design.
Reports 80–85% agreement and says a kappa-style estimate would likely be substantial-to-almost-perfect; lists high-agreement structural and non-structural classifications.
Discusses AlexNet boundary-location disagreement, classifies Transformers structural, and interprets agreement as convergent validity signal overlapping expert intuition.
Explicitly states no live external raters were recruited, so test is not a true blinded expert study; also flags selection bias and specifies requirements for rigorous future version.
Calls result positive validation signal but not proof of correctness; next step is genuine external testing.
Classifies minimax -> alpha-beta pruning as strong candidate; mechanism is pruning branches without changing perfect-condition minimax result, reducing effective search space.
Maps pruning to description-length absorption, increased information per computation and deeper reachable search under same compute.

parse_units.section: Capability Transition + Temporal Validation + Resource Controls
parse_units.content: Claims practical chess-engine impact; reports milestone periods and τ≈decades; source argues alpha-beta is lower-confound structural control despite hardware contributions.
Rates all main criteria positive with low resource confound and concludes alpha-beta provides strong support for CPB mechanism.
Explores consciousness as possible computational phase boundary; explicitly does not resolve subjective experience; proposes self-integrating search-process hypothesis.

References Causal Mass and Computational Phase Boundaries as earlier abstraction steps and gives examples of interface complexity absorption; named external/program endpoints are not repository-resolved by this parse.

parse_units.section: Internal Phase Boundary + Self-Integration + Candidate Conditions
parse_units.content: Proposes many local processes -> unified self-integrating search process; candidate conditions include shared representation, recursive self-modeling, internal search coordination and recursive optimization, each with predictions/measurements.

Proposes ΔI -> ΔR -> ΔS -> ΔA, senses as specialized search agents, and AGI consciousness-like properties as integration rather than raw capability; source labels these possible interpretations/predictions.

Lists consciousness-without-integration, integration-without-consciousness and intelligence-without-self-integration weakening cases; presents Causal Mass -> IICG -> CPB -> consciousness chain; closes that purpose is falsifiable hypothesis, not solved consciousness.
Reports unexpected transfer of CPB lens to a pre-existing music playlist taxonomy; explicitly says this is not evidence CPB is correct and describes taxonomy categories/claimed stability.
Claims CPB changed classification axis from aesthetics/object categories to induced cognitive trajectories and draws process-classification parallel without asserting music/computation equivalence.

parse_units.section: Why This Matters + Candidate General Principle
parse_units.content: Source says cleaner transfer is not validation but may indicate domain-general abstraction; proposes that complex systems may be classified by how they alter exploration dynamics rather than contained objects.

Names IICG and CPB and proposes conceptual bridge; calls playlist taxonomy phenomenological analogue; target IICG is preserved as named referent without endpoint resolution; future test asks whether lens improves classification/decisions in unintended domains.

parse_units.section: Core Mechanism + Capability vs Capability Production
parse_units.content: Synthesizes bottleneck relocation/complexity absorption and distinguishes resource capability scaling from search transformation.
Proposes classifying by induced transformations and notes similar dynamics in cognitive/music systems.

parse_units.section: Compression Necessary but Not Sufficient + Navigation Instrument
parse_units.content: States beautiful compression != useful interface and that strongest demonstrated CPB capability is currently reframing/navigation rather than prediction.

Narrates Causal Mass -> Interface-Induced Computational Geometry -> Computational Phase Boundaries as self-described development/compression trajectory; named framework references are preserved without map endpoint resolution.

parse_units.section: Validation Requirement + Current Core Hypothesis + Open Question
parse_units.content: Requires external transfer that improves others' search behavior; current synthesis defines phase boundary as transformation of exploration mechanism; asks whether CPB itself can become a phase boundary.

parse_units.section: Recursive Criterion + CPB as Cognitive Phase Boundary
parse_units.content: Proposes that framework becomes computationally significant only if it changes future exploration; describes CPB abstraction as reusable analysis pipeline and self-applied complexity absorption.

parse_units.section: Object vs Process Classification + Transformation Invariant
parse_units.content: Contrasts object categories with transformation-induced classification and proposes complexity moves from agent to interface as invariant.
Proposes high-value interaction can create new representation/search space and CPB may be more useful as navigation system than predictive theory.

parse_units.section: Cross-Domain Transfer + Danger of False Compression
parse_units.content: Proposes trajectory-based cross-domain generalization but warns elegant compression without predictions/decisions/exploration improvement is insufficient.

Next stage is operational interface tests for bottleneck detection, intervention generation, reasoning-loop improvement and predictive comparison; framework should be judged by whether it makes discovery easier.

parse_units.section: Core Observation + Systems as Trajectory Generators
parse_units.content: Proposes trajectories/attractors can predict system behavior better than current state and distinguishes observed event from trajectory generator.
Proposes authenticity reduces hidden information needed to predict behavior through stable incentives/values and cross-context coherence.

Relates trajectory coherence to CPB and playlist taxonomy and proposes systems are understood by attractors/trajectories they create; analogies are not represented as identity or scientific dependency.

Proposes A proportional to negative divergence between internal and behavioral distributions, explicitly labels it proposed rather than established measurement, and asks whether authenticity signals predict long-term behavior better than surface behavior.
